scope: Guarded Rocket NPC/item-kit engineering QA. Synthetic inventory fixtures verify controlled edge cases, not organic story progression or release acceptance.

cases.scope: Normal gift quantities are correct; decline preserves the starting bag; repeating the offer does not duplicate gifts.
A synthetic fixture of 60 unique valid key items excludes 114/118. Canonical storage is full before interaction; the no-code offer leaves all 60 unchanged and grants neither custom item.
A synthetic 59/60 bag receives item 114 in its last slot and withholds marker 118. After a separate slot is freed, a no-code retry grants 118 while preserving pre-owned quantities.
Party Healer restores status, HP, and PP. Marker 118 enables Rare Candy reuse; without the marker, ordinary Rare Candy is consumed.
Canonical and native readback: TM 328/329 change from 2/98 to 99/99, absent TM 330 stays 0, and HM 420 stays 1; no active codes.
A fresh process without state input or active codes loads the same battery save. Native inventory persists and Rare Candy remains reusable.
The candidate script body is uniquely loaded and active in RAM and matches the candidate bytes; comparison result is 1.

preserved_runner_snapshot.note: Byte-identical acceptance instrument; this hash is not retroactively attributed to archived runs.

traceability_limitations.input_state_hashes: All 14 archived results without per-run core/runner hashes also lack a recorded input-state hash. The acceptance audit hashes available input files separately without backfilling those records. Newer battery reload runs intentionally have no state input.

limits: Synthetic inventory cases are controlled fixtures, not organic campaign progress.
Runner result PASS means emulation completed; gameplay acceptance comes from the independent assertions in the acceptance record.
The isolated candidate is unpublished and does not replace the accepted download target.
Full story progression, PC inventory, held berries in battle, Escape Rope in a cave, and physical controls remain outside this acceptance.
The EV/IV/Nature editor is a separate feasibility scope and is not implemented in this candidate.
